title: Database queries are plain SQL files loaded with aiosql on the asyncpg driver, not an ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file under app/db/queries/sql with aiosql using the asyncpg adapter. Repositories call these named queries, so new queries must be added as SQL files.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete="SET NULL" and is nullable. Comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE instead, so they are removed with the user.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Only the author may modify or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article returns true only when the article author's username equals the current user's username. The update and delete routes depend on this check and return 403 otherwise.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
security.py builds a CryptContext with the single scheme bcrypt and deprecated="auto". get_password_hash and verify_password both go through this context.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: API models expose snake_case fields as camelCase JSON through an alias generator.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allows population by field name. Datetimes are encoded as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: Article listing defaults to 20 items per page with no upper limit.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0. The query parameter limit is only constrained by ge=1, so a client can request any page size.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: The asyncpg connection pool defaults to a fixed size of 10 connections.
content:
AppSettings sets both max_connection_count and min_connection_count to 10. connect_to_db passes them as max_size and min_size to asyncpg.create_pool at startup.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
The JWT service encodes and decodes every access token with HS256 using the application secret_key. Decoding accepts only this one algorithm, so changing it invalidates all issued tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after they are issued.
content:
create_access_token_for_user sets the token lifetime to ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES, which is 60 * 24 * 7 minutes. There is no refresh token, so users must log in again after a week.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The access token identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
content:
The token payload is built from JWTUser(username=user.username), and the auth dependency looks the user up with get_user_by_username. Renaming a user therefore invalidates their existing tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Creating an article whose slug already exists is rejected with 400.
content:
The create route computes the slug and calls check_article_exists before inserting. If an article with that slug exists it raises 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS, so two articles cannot share a title that slugifies the same way.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

title: A separately stored per-user salt is prepended to the password before hashing.
content:
change_password generates a new salt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same stored salt, so the salt column and the concatenation order must stay in sync.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The update route recomputes the slug whenever a new title is sent, so the article URL changes with its title.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token". The auth dependency splits the Authorization header on a space and returns 403 if the prefix does not match this setting.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT. It raises that error both when no user has the email and when check_password fails.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(). BEFORE UPDATE triggers attach it to the users, articles and commentaries tables.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
